entries.title: La noche triste de Trump | Noticias
entries.paragraph_1: Como nos advirtió Heráclito, en este universo nada es permanente, pero incluso el filósofo griego se habría sorprendido ante la rapidez con la que cambian las cosas en el mundo político actual en que lo que un día parece inevitable puede esfumarse por  completo el siguiente. Hace apenas dos años, muchos analistas norteamericanos daban por moribundo al Partido Demócrata, cuya candidata, Kamala Harris, acababa de sufrir una contundente derrota en la contienda presidencial frente a un resurgido Donald Trump. Sin embargo, a pesar de seguir divididos y sin darse el trabajo de modificar sus propuestas, los demócratas lograron recuperarse lo suficiente como para cosechar una victoria espectacular en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de la semana pasada.
entries.paragraph_2: Desde entonces, quienes predijeron la inminente desaparición del Partido Demócrata están diciendo prácticamente lo mismo sobre el Republicano y, claro está, sobre el propio Trump, para quien los resultados fueron un desastre absoluto. Durante al menos los próximos dos años, demócratas sedientos de revancha, cuyo odio y desprecio hacia Trump no conocen límites, controlarán ambas cámaras del Congreso. Algunos intentarán someterlo a un juicio político con la esperanza de destituirlo, otros se conformarán con hacer todo lo posible por obligarlo a suavizar su postura en cuestiones como la inmigración ilegal -algo que, para sorpresa de muchos, dice estar dispuesto a hacer-, además de cohonestar las cuotas raciales destinadas a favorecer a minorías étnicas, garantizar los derechos adquiridas de las personas transexuales y otros temas que obsesionan a los activistas.

entries.paragraph_1: According to a report by Taipei Times, the Taiwanese Foreign Ministry made the remarks after China issued a statement following talks between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema on Friday. The Chinese statement highlighted Gabons reaffirmation of its adherence to the one China principle. Taiwans MOFA criticised the statement, accusing Beijing of distorting United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758 to advance its political claims over Taiwan. UN General Assembly Resolution 2758, adopted in 1971, addresses China's representation at the United Nations and does not explicitly mention Taiwan. However, Beijing interprets the resolution as granting it the right to represent Taiwan. As cited by Taipei Times, MOFA accused the Chinese government of repeatedly using bilateral meetings with other countries to pressure them into issuing statements that undermine the sovereignty of the Republic of China. Reaffirming Taiwan's position, the ministry said the ROC is a sovereign and independent country and that Taiwan has never been ruled by the People's Republic of China (PRC). It further maintained that only Taiwan's democratically elected government has the authority to represent its people in international affairs, including within the United Nations system. The Taiwanese Foreign Ministry also accused Beijing of attempting to undermine the international order by incorporating its one China principle into bilateral documents signed with other countries. MOFA urged Gabon not to fall for what it described as Beijing's political manipulation, stressing that the political status of Taiwan cannot be altered through China's diplomatic pressure or unilateral claims. The ministry reiterated that the two sides of the Taiwan Strait are not subordinate to each other, describing this as an established fact that cannot be changed. (ANI)

entries.title: Taiwan says China is conducting ’area denial’ drills in Western Pacific  - International | Daily Mirror
entries.paragraph_1: Middleast Lankadeepa
entries.paragraph_2: (Reuters) - China is carrying out "area denial" drills in the Western Pacific ‌involving one of its aircraft carriers and other naval formations, Taiwan Defence Minister Wellington Koo said on Tuesday, following a reported rise in Chinese activities. China, which views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory, regularly sends its ​warplanes and warships into the skies and waters around the island. Last week, Taiwan National Security ​Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu posted on his X account details of the ⁠deployments of more than 100 Chinese naval and Coast Guard ships operating off Taiwan, in the ​South China Sea, and into the Pacific. Taiwan's defence ministry last week also reported a large rise ​in the number of Chinese air force aircraft around Taiwan, though China has not formally declared any drills. "China has indeed conducted area denial drills in the Western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group and other naval training formations," ​Koo told reporters at parliament. Anti-access/area denial, or A2AD, refers to keeping an outside force from ​intervening in a conflict, which in the Taiwan context means stopping US or other allied forces from coming to ‌Taipei's ⁠aid should Beijing attack. China's defence ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The ministry said last month that the Liaoning carrier's training in the western Pacific was an annual routine to test long-range, open-ocean combat capabilities and was not directed at any particular country. China's drills come ahead of ​both the APEC summit ​in Shenzhen next week, ⁠where US President Donald Trump is expected to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping again, and Taiwan's local elections at the end of this month. Koo ​said the military was keeping a close watch on what China was ​up to. "We ⁠believe that this kind of military deterrence is intended to undermine peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific region," he added. "We will use joint intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance means and exchange intelligence with allies to ⁠continuously ​monitor these activities and respond appropriately." China has never renounced the ​use of force to bring Taiwan under its control, though it says it would prefer "peaceful reunification". Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty ​claims, saying only the Taiwanese people can decide their future.

entries.paragraph_2: Paris [France] November 12 (ANI): Foreign ministers of the Group of Seven ( G7 ) have expressed concern over China 's increasingly assertive activities in the waters east of Taiwan , warning that the actions threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and the safety of international shipping, according to a report by Taipei Times. The warning was issued in a joint declaration published late Wednesday following a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris. According to the report, China , which claims Taiwan as part of its territory, has intensified its activities off Taiwan 's east coast since June, conducting regular patrols by its coast guard. Taiwan ese officials believe Beijing is practising for a potential maritime blockade by deploying overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets in the surrounding waters. The G7 statement marked a unified expression of concern over China 's activities east of Taiwan . France, Germany, the United Kingdom and the United States had previously voiced concerns about Beijing 's actions in the area. entries.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO by board - Times of Oman
entries.paragraph_1: New Delhi : Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has opted to resign amidst mounting pressure, reported Reuters. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as Nvidia looks for a permanent successor, the company said on Thursday. Huang has been in the eye of a storm after it was revealed that he had an affair with Alice Huang (not his relation) a Chinese businesswoman who is alleged to be a intelligence asset. Jensen Huang was also reported have had another affair with a senior executive of Nvidia Kimberly Powell. Jensen Huang had acknowledged his affair with Alice Huang in a letter to Nvidia employees where he apologised for being unfaithful to his wife and violating her trust. Nvidia's board had also initiated an investigation into the matter, with the inquiry being led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. In May 2026 a Wall Street 'Short seller' Culper research had flagged Huang's alleged links to Alice Huang. According to CBS News, on May 13 this year Culper Research published a 40-page report highlighting Huang's ties to Alice Huang, a former television reporter and financial industry executive. According to the report, a copy of which is with ANI, Culper research said, "Nvidia has repeatedly vouched for Megaspeed – its single largest Southeast Asian chip buyer currently under investigation by both U.S. Commerce and Singapore authorities." "Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has not only vouched for Megaspeed, but seems to have quite literally walked alongside Megaspeed at every step, while maintaining an uncomfortably close relationship with Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, a Chinese national. He was first spotted partying with Alice Huang in June 2024 – the same month the Apex/Alibaba pledge was filed. He then dined with Alice Huang in Taiwan in May 2025 – just weeks after the news of U.S. trade restrictions. Finally, per one current Megaspeed employee, Jensen visits Megaspeed-linked data centers “every few months” and “every single time” he visits, he is accompanied by representatives from Alibaba. The Megaspeed employee characterised their relationship with Jensen as “very close”, corroborating another former Nvidia employee’s suggestion to us that many Nvidia employees wondered if there was a special relationship," the report stated. Although Jensen Huang had got the backing of US President Donald Trump he was under extreme pressure with members of the US Congress flagging potential security risk of the affair with the alleged spy. Jensen Huang's exit puts the $4 trillion Nvidia in troubled waters and could potentially disrupt the AI industry which has been facing headwinds on the markets recently.

entries.title: Taiwan monitors China's 'area denial' exercises as naval activity intensifies - The Times of India
Taiwan detects 4 PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels operating near territory
entries.paragraph_1: According to an official update shared by the MND on social media platform X, "4 sorties of PLA aircraft, 6 PLAN vessels and 2 official ships operating around Taiwan detected up until 6 a.m. (UTC+8) today. According to the ministry, two of the four aircraft sorties crossed the median line and entered Taiwans southwestern Air Defence Identification Zone (ADIZ), which was monitored and responded to by the Republic of China (ROC) Armed Forces. 2 out of 4 sorties entered Taiwans southwestern part ADIZ. #ROCArmedForces have monitored the situation and responded," the ministry posted. Earlier on November 3, Taiwan accused the China Coast Guard of harassing ships off its eastern coast and attempting to assert what it described as fictional jurisdiction over the surrounding waters, as Beijing continues to increase its maritime patrols around the island, according to a report by Taipei Times. The report said Taiwans Coast Guard Administration (CGA) had dispatched vessels, including the Ji An, to monitor Chinese coast guard activity in the area. The Chinese patrols reportedly included the vessels Hushi (CCG 1308) and Meishan (CCG 2303). According to the CGA, China has stepped up its presence off Taiwans east coast since June, conducting regular coast guard patrols. Taiwanese officials have expressed concern that the activity could serve as preparation for a potential maritime blockade, involving overlapping military, paramilitary and civilian assets. Taipei considers the waters off its eastern coast strategically important, particularly for maintaining wartime supply routes in the event of a blockade or military conflict. As cited by Taipei Times, Chinese state media recently released footage showing a vessel broadcasting a radio message claiming to be conducting law enforcement operations and offering assistance if required. Although the intended recipient of the message was not identified, the footage showed an unidentified fishing trawler. Responding to China's activities, the CGA reiterated that the Republic of China (ROC) is a sovereign and independent country, maintaining that the ROC and the People's Republic of China are not subordinate to each other. The agency said China's attempts to harass vessels through radio communications represented an expansion of power that violated international law and undermined regional peace and stability. It also asserted that Taiwan holds sovereign rights and jurisdiction over the exclusive economic zone east of the island, adding that China has no jurisdiction over Taiwan's waters. The CGA further accused Beijing of spreading disinformation through political rhetoric, including referring to Taiwan as Chinas Taiwan Island and describing its maritime activities as law enforcement patrols. It said such claims distorted reality and would not be recognised by the international community. The agency said it would continue monitoring maritime developments and take all necessary measures to safeguard Taiwan's sovereignty and ensure the security of its waters. The Taipei Times report also highlighted China's activity near the Taiwan-controlled Pratas Islands, also known as the Dongsha Islands. The CGA said Beijing had sent another coast guard vessel close to the islands on Saturday, adding that Taiwan had expelled Chinese Coast Guard vessels from Pratas waters 13 times so far this year. Located more than 400 kilometres from Taiwan, the Pratas Islands are considered vulnerable to a potential Chinese attack because of their geographical distance from the main island, according to the report. Meanwhile, speaking at a security forum in Taipei on Saturday, Ocean Affairs Council specialist Pai Pang-ting said Beijing was using multiple types of vessels to challenge Taiwan's maritime law enforcement and administrative jurisdiction. Pai noted that while the Chinese People's Liberation Army maintains a highly visible military presence, Beijing also deploys coast guard, research and fishing vessels to challenge Taiwan's authority at sea. According to Pai, Beijing is attempting to portray repeated incursions as routine administrative management, gradually narrowing Taiwan's ability to exercise jurisdiction over its waters. (ANI)

entries.paragraph_1: The MAGA movement of Donald Trump could find itself confronted with a fresh electoral crushing in 2028 , if the American president fails to curb the high cost of living in the US . Russia , Iran , and China possess the ability to maintain economic pressures on American society, damaging the political prospects of the Republicans. To avert such a contingency, Trump will need to proceed with a series of grand mutual compromise deals, satisfying some of the most sensitive geopolitical interests of the three nations. The heavy defeat recently suffered by the Republicans may be repeated in the elections of 2028 , if Trump fails to reduce the cost of living, which surged over the past year due to the Third Gulf War. It has already been pointed out that the American president must curb energy exports toward Europe , if he wants MAGA to preserve its chances for electoral survival in 2028 . Redirecting larger volumes of energy commodities toward the domestic market of the US could contribute to a swifter easing of fuel prices. Concurrently, resolving both the Third Gulf War and the Ukrainian conflict is considered of decisive importance for the gradual restoration of stability across international energy markets. However, even under the most favorable scenario, in which all three of these developments are set in motion by early 2027 , leading to a substantial reduction in fuel prices within the following year and, by extension, the cost of living prior to the elections of 2028 , the outcome may prove temporary.

entries.paragraph_1: عمون - ذكرت أربعة مصادر مطلعة أن مسؤولين يابانيين حذروا شركات الدفاع من تخفيضات كبيرة في الطلبيات المتوقعة، في ​ظل ضغوط مالية تهدد بتقليص خطط تعزيز القدرات العسكرية التي تقول ‌حكومة رئيسة الوزراء ساناي تاكايتشي إنها ضرورية لمواجهة الصين. وأوضحت المصادر المطلعة لرويترز أن مسؤولين في وزارة المالية اقترحوا الأسبوع الماضي تخصيص ما بين 50 تريليون و60 تريليون ين (313 مليارا ​إلى 376 مليار دولار) للإنفاق الدفاعي على مدى خمس سنوات، بداية ​من أبريل نيسان 2027. ورغم أن هذا المبلغ يزيد على المخصصات البالغة ⁠43 تريليون ين في الخطة الخمسية الحالية، فإنه يقل بكثير عن ميزانية ​بقيمة 80 تريليون ين كان بعض مسؤولي الدفاع ونواب الحزب الديمقراطي الحر الحاكم ​قد افترضوها واستخدموها في مفاوضاتهم مع شركات الدفاع. وقالت المصادر، التي طلبت عدم الكشف عن هوياتها لعدم حصولها على تفويض بالحديث إلى وسائل الإعلام حول هذا الأمر، إن خفض الإنفاق المقترح ​ربما يؤدي إلى تقليص المشتريات المخطط لها من بعض الصواريخ والطائرات سواء ​من موردين محليين أم أجانب، بنسب تصل إلى النصف، ويشمل ذلك مقاتلات إف-35 أمريكية الصنع. وقال ‌متحدث ⁠باسم وزارة الدفاع "لم يتم اتخاذ أي قرار بعد بشأن حجم خطة تعزيز الدفاع المقبلة. موقفنا هو اتخاذ القرار بشأن ما تحتاجه اليابان لدفاعها، ثم وضع الميزانية بناء على ذلك". ووفقا لحسابات رويترز، فإن الإنفاق المقترح الذي يصل إلى 60 تريليون ​ين يعني أن اليابان ​لن تحقق هدف ⁠رفع الإنفاق الدفاعي إلى اثنين بالمئة من الناتج المحلي الإجمالي، وذلك في وقت يضغط فيه الرئيس الأمريكي دونالد ترامب ​على حلفاء واشنطن لزيادة إنفاقهم على جيوشهم. وتطالب استراتيجية الدفاع الوطني ​الأمريكية ⁠لعام 2026 الحلفاء في جميع أنحاء العالم بإنفاق 3.5 بالمئة من الناتج المحلي الإجمالي على قواتهم المسلحة و1.5 بالمئة إضافية على الاحتياجات الأمنية الأوسع نطاقا. وتعمل اليابان على ⁠تعزيز قدراتها ​العسكرية لمواجهة القوة العسكرية الصينية المتنامية، وسط ​مخاوف بشأن احتمال شن الصين هجوما على تايوان. وتشعر طوكيو بالقلق من أن مثل هذا الصراع يمكن ​أن يهدد جزرها المجاورة وممراتها البحرية الحيوية. entries.paragraph_1: Chinese President Xi Jinping has reiterated Beijing's determination to bring Taiwan under its control, declaring that the island's eventual reunification with mainland China is inevitable, even as Taipei rejected his proposal and warned against accepting Communist Party rule.
entries.paragraph_2: Addressing an event commemorating the 160th birth anniversary of revolutionary leader Sun Yat-sen in Beijing on Thursday, Xi said China's reunification was an unfinished historical responsibility that would eventually be fulfilled.

entries.title: Acer founder Stan Shih named Taiwan's envoy to 2026 APEC summit - Focus Taiwan
entries.paragraph_1: Taipei, Nov. 11 (CNA) Acer Group founder and Honorary Chairman Stan Shih (施振榮) has been named Taiwan's envoy to the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China, the Presidential Office said on Wednesday.
entries.paragraph_2: President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) chose Shih for his international perspective and industry expertise, hoping he would bring Taiwan's views and experience on economic and trade issues to the summit, Presidential Office spokesperson Karen Kuo (郭雅慧) said.

entries.title: Taiwan denuncia exercícios militares chineses de "negação de área" no Pacífico ocidental
entries.paragraph_1: A China está a realizar exercícios militares de negação de área no Pacífico ocidental, com a participação do grupo de combate do porta-aviões Liaoning e de outras formações navais, afirmou hoje o ministro da Defesa de Taiwan.
entries.paragraph_2: Em declarações citadas pela agência de notícias taiwanesa CNA, Wellington Koo denunciou que a "dissuasão militar" chinesa "visa minar a paz e a estabilidade" na região do Indo-Pacífico, sublinhando que as autoridades de Taiwan mantêm um "controlo rigoroso" da situação.
